title: Ex power
goal: Edit many lines at once from the command line: ranges, :g, :normal, :sort, :t/:m, shell filters and number increments.

lessons.title: Ranges, :t and :m

concepts.desc: run an Ex command on lines N to M.
current line / last line / the whole file (same as 1,$).
offsets: from here to 3 lines down; the last three lines.
from the next line matching pat1 to the next line matching pat2 (both searched from the cursor).
between marks a and b; the last visual selection (typing : in visual mode inserts it).
:5t. copies line 5 below the cursor; :m0 moves the current line to the top; :3m1 puts line 3 after line 1.

lessons.tip: With line numbers on, :12,18d is often faster than moving there and counting. :t. (duplicate the line) beats yyp when you're not on that line.

quiz.q: Delete lines 10 through 20.
What range means 'from the current line to the end of the file'?
Copy line 7 to just below the cursor.
Move the current line to the top of the file.
What does `:/start/,/end/d` do?
quiz.a: Deletes from the next line matching 'start' through the next line matching 'end'.

quiz.q: You select lines in visual mode and press `:`. What appears, and what does it mean?
quiz.a: :'<,'> - a range covering the selected lines.

lessons.title: :g and :v

concepts.desc: run an Ex command on every line matching pat.
run it on every line NOT matching pat.
delete all blank lines.
move matching lines to the end, keeping their order.
run normal-mode keys on each matching line.
an empty pattern in :s reuses pat.

lessons.tip: :v/keep/d is the fastest 'grep in place': it keeps only the lines you care about. u undoes the whole :g in one go.

quiz.q: Delete every line containing DEBUG.
Delete every line that does NOT contain 'error'.
Delete all empty lines.
What does `:g/^import/m0` do to the order of the import lines?
quiz.a: Moves them to the top in reverse order (each one goes to line 0 in turn).

quiz.q: Add a semicolon to the end of every line containing 'let'.
How many undo steps does one :g command take?
quiz.a: One - a single u undoes it all.

lessons.title: :normal and :sort

concepts.desc: run normal-mode keys on each line of the range, starting at column 0.
append ; to every line.
repeat the last change on each selected line.
sort lines / in reverse.
drop duplicates / sort by the first number / ignore case.
sort by what comes after the match (e.g. :sort /,/ sorts by the second CSV field).

lessons.tip: Without a range, :sort sorts the whole file. Select a block with vip first and :sort only touches that block.

quiz.q: Comment out lines 5-9 with `// ` using :normal.
Sort the selected lines and drop duplicates.
Why does `:sort` put '100' before '9', and how do you fix it?
quiz.a: It sorts as text; :sort n sorts numerically.

quiz.q: Sort the whole file in reverse order.
What does `:%norm .` do?
quiz.a: Repeats the last change on every line of the file.

quiz.q: Where does :normal start on each line?
quiz.a: At the start of the line (column 0), in normal mode.

lessons.title: Shell filters and Ctrl-a

concepts.desc: send the lines through a shell command and replace them with its output (:%!sort, :1,5!uniq).
the same from normal mode: !ip opens :.,.+N! for the paragraph, then type the command.
insert a command's output / a file's contents below the cursor.
add / subtract 1 from the number at or after the cursor. Takes a count: 5 Ctrl-a.
on a selection, make a sequence: the first line +1, the second +2, and so on.

lessons.tip: Any Unix tool becomes a vim command: :%!sort -u, :'<,'>!column -t, :.!date. Ctrl-a searches forward for the number, so you rarely need to move onto it.

quiz.q: Sort the whole file with the shell's sort.
Insert the output of `ls` below the cursor.
Add 10 to the number under or after the cursor.
Five lines say `item 0`. Turn them into item 1 to item 5.
quiz.a: Select them with V, then g Ctrl-a.

quiz.q: What does `!ip` start?
quiz.a: A filter over the inner paragraph: :.,.+N! is typed for you and you add the command.

quiz.q: Decrease a number by 1.

lessons.title: Week 8 review

concepts.desc: ranges
act on matching / non-matching lines
bulk line editing
shell filters and numbers

lessons.tip: Before writing a macro, ask whether a :g or :norm over a range does the job in one line.

quiz.q: Duplicate the current line without yanking it.
Move every line containing 'done' to the end of the file.
Append ',' to lines 3-8.
Sort lines 2-10 numerically.
Uppercase the whole file with a shell filter.
Comment out the last two lines with `# `.
